messages.subject: errnoException
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to install Shiny Server.

1) I have set up a virtual machine running RHEL 5 (I used VirtualBox on Windows 7), and then I have installed the Shiny Server on the Linux RHEL 5 machine.
2) I copied the 01_hello example (containing ui.R, and server.R) in the folder /srv/shiny-server
3) I then open a root terminal and run sudo /sbin/service shiny-server start
4) when I do ps -a the shiny-server shows up in the running processes
5) I then go to my Windows machine and open a Chrome web browser and type http://<ipaddress>:3838/01_hello where the <ipaddress> is the IP address of my Linux virtual machine

This produces the following exception on the server:

/opt/shiny-server/lib/main.js:313
   throw err;
         ^
Error: write EPIP
      at errnoException (net.js:901:11)
      at Object.afterWrite (net.js:718:19)

Could you guys help?

Thank you so much,
Jules

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: errnoException
parts:
Jules,

I was able to reproduce your issue, and might have a workaround for you.

In my case since I build R locally, my executable script is in /usr/local/bin/R (this is what "which R" command returns). Shiny Server is not finding R in this location. But if I create a symlink to this location as "/usr/bin/R", then Shiny Server will find R. 

This is the command I used, and you could adjust it for your location of R:

sudo ln -s /usr/local/bin/R /usr/bin/R     

See if this workaround fixes your problem. And we will look into fixing the issue on our end.

Fereshteh

I should also mention (for reference) that you can define the path to R on your system within the startup script.

For CentOS 5:

Modify this script: /etc/init.d/shiny-server 

and add a line like this to the beginning of script:

export R=/path/to/R
